Issues.Title: fix(core): replay events dispatched while a block is already hydrating
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When a trigger that does not replay events, such as `hydrate on viewport`, `on idle` or `on timer`, starts hydrating a block, an event dispatched inside that block before the hydration completes is lost.

Event replay queues the event and calls `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` with a replay callback, but the function returns early because the block is already in the `hydrating` registry. The hydration that is already running was started without a replay callback, so nothing ever replays the queued event.

In practice, the first click on content that has just scrolled into view does nothing, and the user has to click again. The window is as long as it takes to load the block's dependencies and render it, so it widens on slow connections. I hit it in an app with a button inside a `@defer (on viewport; hydrate on viewport)` block: tabbing to the button scrolls it into view, and pressing Enter straight away lost the press in 20 of 36 runs under load.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

An event that arrives while another trigger is hydrating its block waits for that hydration to finish and is then replayed, the same way the event path replays after a hydration it started itself. If the block fails to hydrate, its content is cleaned up and there is nothing to replay the event on, so it is dropped, as before.

The new test starts hydration through the viewport trigger, dispatches a click on the still dehydrated content, and expects the handler to have run exactly once. Without the change, the block hydrates but the counter stays at 0.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

I could not run the Bazel suite on my machine (Windows). Instead I ran `incremental_hydration_spec.ts` and `event_replay_spec.ts` from the 22.2.x branch with Jasmine against the published 22.2.0 packages, with the same change applied to the FESM bundle: 46 of 46 and 23 of 23 pass. Without the change, the new test is the only failure.

Issues.Title: refactor(docs-infra): use resource() to highlight code in the home page code block
Issues.Body:
The home page code block created a new Promise in a `computed` whenever the code, language or theme changed, and unwrapped it with the `async` pipe.

Issues.Title: Provide an option to control template access to TypeScript private members
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler

### Description

Follow-up to the discussion in #70514, filed as agreed there.

Since #70188, templates can access members declared `private` on the component class. The motivation given in #70188 is specific: under `isolatedDeclarations: true`, template-facing members declared `protected` require explicit type annotations, and allowing `private` removes that requirement. The behaviour change, however, applies to every Angular component, whether or not `isolatedDeclarations` is used.

For existing codebases this lands implicitly. On upgrade, every `private` member already written becomes reachable from the template at once. Nothing breaks at runtime, but the boundary a declaration expresses and the boundary the compiler enforces no longer match, and they stay mismatched until the codebase has been migrated to whatever the new convention is. There is no diagnostic to surface this, and the style guide still recommends `protected` for template-facing members.

JS `#private` elements remain inaccessible from templates, but only because of a runtime limitation. If class and template are meant to be one cohesive unit, that argument covers `#private` too, so it is not clear this is a boundary teams should build on. A related question raised in #70514 is whether, with the TypeScript 7 compiler, `.ngtypecheck.ts` files are still generated in the same way, which also bears on how stable the current behaviour is.

As it stands, upgrading to 22.2 and committing to a new convention for member visibility cannot be separated. An option would let them happen in that order, on the team's own schedule.

### Proposed solution

An `angularCompilerOptions` flag that controls whether templates may access `private` members. Following @PapaNappa's suggestion in #70514:

```jsonc
"angularCompilerOptions": {
  // "auto" (default) | "allow" | "disallow"
  "privateAccessFromTemplates": "auto"
}
```

- `auto` derives the behaviour from `isolatedDeclarations`: allowed when it is enabled, disallowed when it is not. This keeps the benefit for the codebases the change was aimed at, and leaves the previous semantics in place elsewhere.
- `allow` and `disallow` let a team opt in or out explicitly, independently of `isolatedDeclarations`.

@PowerKiKi suggested a simpler variant: no new flag, and template access to `private` members permitted only when `isolatedDeclarations` is enabled. That would also address the problem, at the cost of not being separately controllable.

A lighter alternative would be an opt-in diagnostic that reports template access to `private` members, leaving the behaviour unchanged. That is enough to keep a convention enforceable, though it does not restore the previous semantics.

### Alternatives considered

**Migrate template-facing members to `private` and hidden members to `#private`.** This is the smallest change, and mostly automatable. It depends on `#private` remaining inaccessible from templates, which is not documented. It also has known friction: `#private` members cannot be reached from tests the way `private` ones can via `component['member']`, and `private` members used only in templates are reported as unused (TS6133).

**Move anything the template must not reach off the component**, into an injected ViewModel, Facade or Store. This keeps the boundary regardless of how member visibility is treated, but it is a design change in every affected component rather than a rename, and it is disproportionate for small components.

**Adopt the new behaviour as is.** Viable for new code. For an existing codebase it means accepting a mismatch between declared and enforced visibility across the whole codebase for the duration of the migration, with no tooling to track progress.

**An external lint rule.** Angular ESLint could in principle flag template access to `private` members. This would live outside the compiler and could drift from its semantics, and it does not help teams that do not use it.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Provide an option to control template access to TypeScript private members" (#71066)

Issues.Title: fix(docs-infra): guard against duplicate error transitions in node runtime sandbox
Issues.Body:
When `startInteractiveTerminal` encounters an out-of-memory error, `setErrorState` is invoked, setting the error state, terminating the web container, and decrementing the sandbox instance counter.

However, `init` previously proceeded to `initProject`, which called `installDependencies` and set the loading step to `INSTALL`. This overwrote `LoadingStep.ERROR`, causing the secondary failure on the terminated container to re-enter `setErrorState` and decrement the instance counter a second time.

Add checks to `init`, `setLoading`, and `setErrorState` for existing errors to prevent re-entering error handling and overwriting the error state.

Issues.Title: fix(core): respect detach() on views attached to ApplicationRef
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Calling `detach()` on a view that is attached directly to `ApplicationRef` has no effect. `detach()` only clears the `Attached` flag, and that flag is only read when a view is reached through its parent. Root views are where the traversal starts, so they get checked anyway:

- Eager component or embedded view: checked on every `tick()`
- OnPush component: checked after `markForCheck()`
- zoneless: checked when a signal read in the template changes

The same component created through a `ViewContainerRef` respects `detach()`, and so does the `ChangeDetectorRef` injected inside the component (it points to the component view, not the root view).

The only way out today is `appRef.detachView()`, but the code calling `detach()` usually doesn't know the view is attached to `ApplicationRef`, and it also removes the view from the DOM.

Issue Number: #46690

## What is the new behavior?

`ApplicationRef` skips detached views:

- when refreshing views
- in the dev mode `checkNoChanges` pass
- when deciding if another pass is needed, otherwise a dirty detached view would keep requesting passes until `synchronize` gives up with NG0103

`detectChanges()` on a detached view still checks it, and `reattach()` brings it back to regular change detection.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

This matches what `detach()` documents, but it is a behavior change for anyone calling `detach()` on a root view and relying on it still being checked. Happy to change the target or add a note if you think that's needed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(core): respect detach() on views attached to ApplicationRef" (#71062)

Issues.Title: fix(router): require outlets to match a route before processing child…
Issues.Body:
… segments

Previously, empty-path outlet groups in a request URL (such as `x:/(detail:2)`, `///(detail:2)`, or `x:/()`) were allowed to match without a corresponding route for that outlet name in the route configuration:

1. `processChildren` called `processSegmentGroup` for each child outlet, which immediately delegated any zero-segment group with children back to `processChildren` against the same parent `config` and `parentRoute` without matching a route. Calling `processSegment` directly in `processChildren` ensures only the root `UrlSegmentGroup` short-circuits to `processChildren`.
2. `processSegmentAgainstRoute` allowed named outlets to match leaf empty-path routes for other outlets even when those routes had no children that could contain the target outlet.
3. `matchSegmentAgainstRoute` branched into `processChildren` or returned a completed leaf match before `getOutlet(route) === outlet` was satisfied, and did not require a descendant `TreeNode` match when piercing an empty-path route for a different outlet.
4. `noLeftoversInUrl` only checked `!segmentGroup.children[outlet]` rather than `!segmentGroup.hasChildren() && outlet === PRIMARY_OUTLET`, allowing unmatched zero-segment outlet groups in the URL to be treated as having no leftovers instead of throwing `NoMatch`.

Together, these allowed crafted URLs with unconfigured zero-segment outlet groups to fan out across empty-path routes (#70932) or repeatedly evaluate guards and construct duplicate route snapshot subtrees across sibling outlets (#70997). Requiring every child segment group to match a route for its outlet before unwrapping children or completing a match prevents the invalid matches at the source.

Fixes #70932
Fixes #70997

Issues.Title: refactor(docs-infra): drive the progress bar from the `currentNavigation` signal
Issues.Body:
The progress bar listened to `NavigationStart` on `router.events`, started a timer to show the bar after `PROGRESS_BAR_DELAY`, and used `switchMap` to wait for the first `NavigationEnd`/`Cancel`/`Skipped`/`Error` event to clear the timer and complete the bar.

Replace this with a single `effect` on the router's `currentNavigation` signal: while a navigation is ongoing the effect schedules the timer, and its cleanup, which runs when the navigation ends or is superseded, clears the timer and completes the bar. The effect tracks the navigation id rather than the navigation object, since `currentNavigation` notifies on every update of an ongoing navigation and would otherwise restart the timer mid-navigation.

Replace the disabled spec with specs that keep a navigation pending through a resolver, covering slow, fast and canceled navigations.

Issues.Title: Nested `&` selectors inside `:host` get `_ngcontent` attribute and no longer match (regression in 22.2.0)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

Since d0d7f57e08 (#69885, "fix(compiler): scope nested CSS rules"), selectors nested with `&` inside a `:host` rule are scoped with the content attribute. `&` there refers to the host element, which only has the `_nghost-*` attribute, so the rule never matches.

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-avatar',
  host: { class: 'md' },
  template: '',
  styles: `
    :host {
      display: block;
      &.md { width: 70px; }
    }
  `,
})
export class Avatar {}
```

Output of the emulated encapsulation:

| Version | Output                                                         |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 22.1.8  | `[_nghost-c1] { display: block; &.md { width: 70px; } }`             |
| 22.2.0  | `[_nghost-c1] { display: block; &.md[_ngcontent-c1] { width: 70px; } }` |

In 22.2.0 the rule resolves to `[_nghost-c1].md[_ngcontent-c1]`. The host element carries `_nghost-c1` and its *parent's* `_ngcontent-*`, so `&.md` no longer applies.

Minimal repro with the compiler directly:

```js
import { encapsulateStyle } from '@angular/compiler';
encapsulateStyle(':host { &.md { width: 70px } }', 'c1');
// 22.1.8: [_nghost-c1] { &.md { width: 70px } }
// 22.2.0: [_nghost-c1] { &.md[_ngcontent-c1] { width: 70px } }
```

Issues.Title: perf(devtools): use HTML canvas for the highlighter
Issues.Body:
The existing highlighting mechanism relies on DOM elements. This has some implications like introducing layout thrashing since each highlight adds/removes elements to and from the DOM tree. This change converts the highlighter to an HTML canvas renderer which should introduce minimal performance overhead when adding and removing overlays, which is especially important for the change detection highlighting considering we want to affect the inspected app as little as possible. 

### Changes overview
- The `Highlight` public API is almost unchanged, so the users of the highlighter are almost unaffected. There is some refactoring on that side like putting the highlight templates in a separate file, for example.
- There is a new `Renderer` that substitutes the old DOM util functions in `dom.ts`. Each `Highlight` instance keeps a ref to the global highlighter renderer. The renderer itself orchestrates the canvas changes.
- `RenderOp`s contain the blueprints and the canvas instructions on how to render the highlights. Right now, we have 2 types of ops – a static and a dynamic one (for the fading-out highlights). The mechanism allows for extension of other types of operations/highlights, if they are needed in the future.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular-devkit/build-angular): do not mark standalone expression statements as pure
Issues.Body:
Top-level call and new expressions that appear directly as expression statements are executed solely for their side effects, such as class property initialization, static blocks, and helper calls.

When targeting browsers requiring class static block or property lowering (e.g., Chrome < 94), Babel's preset-env lowers self-referencing static properties into zero-argument IIFEs (and static blocks into _staticBlock() calls). Because pure-toplevel-functions previously only skipped IIFEs if they had arguments, zero-argument IIFE statements were marked as pure. Downstream minifiers (such as esbuild) then eliminated these standalone pure statements as dead code, dropping essential class members like Injector.ɵprov and causing NG0201 at bootstrap.

This change ensures that call and new expressions that are directly expression statements are never annotated as pure, avoiding accidental elimination of side-effecting statements without requiring hardcoded whitelists of helper function names.

Fixes #34017

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #33467

Schema says `include` is relative to project root. Code resolves it from source root. So for a library with secondary entry point next to `src` nothing reaches it - `my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts`, `./my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts`, `my-sub-package/my-sub.spec.ts`, `projects/my-lib/my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts` all find zero files and run still says success. Happens with no config too, `ng generate library` writes no `include`.

## What is the new behavior?

Pattern that matched nothing under source root gets retried from project root. Pattern that already matched is not retried, so `**/*.spec.ts` stays where it is and does not start picking up specs outside `src`. Project rooted at workspace root is never retried, that would search every project.

Checked on generated workspace with library, secondary entry point and an `e2e/` spec. Four spellings above fixed plus reporter's `["**/*.spec.ts", "my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts"]`. Six spellings that work today return same files. `e2e/` spec not picked up before or after.

Cost is globbing per pattern instead of batching, needed to tell unmatched from matched. On library with 302 specs medians are 451ms before and 447ms after, spread between rounds is wider than that.

`builders/karma/find-tests.ts` untouched, it calls through without new argument so karma keeps current behavior.

Three of five new cases fail without the change. Other two pin what must not move.

Since the inliner only performs string translation replacements using AST locations already discovered via OXC, the full Babel transformation and compiler tooling bundle is unnecessary.

Issues.Title: unit-test builder (Vitest, 22.2.0 OXC linker): ReferenceError on class referenced by name before its own declaration in a partially-compiled npm library
Issues.Body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

Not sure — this may be a regression introduced by the linker rewrite in 22.2.0 ("migrate Angular Linker to oxc-parser and magic-string"), since I have not tested this with 22.1.x.

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When running `ng test` with the `@angular/build:unit-test` builder (Vitest runner) on Angular CLI / @angular/build 22.2.0, several test files fail to load at all (0 tests reported, whole suite crashes) with:

ReferenceError: Cannot access 'CascadeSelect' before initialization
at CascadeSelectSub.<static_initializer> node_modules/@openng/src/cascadeselect/cascadeselect.ts:131:30


I traced this to the actual shipped file (the path above is a sourcemap reference, not a real file on disk):
`node_modules/@openng/optimus-ui/fesm2022/openng-optimus-ui-cascadeselect.mjs`

In that file, `CascadeSelectSub` is declared at line 176, and its static Ivy partial declaration at line 274 includes:

```js
static ɵfac = i0.ɵɵngDeclareFactory({ ..., type: CascadeSelectSub, deps: [{ token: CascadeSelect }], target: i0.ɵɵFactoryTarget.Component });
```

`CascadeSelect` (the referenced class) is not declared until line 452, further down in the same file. Since this is emitted as a literal `class` declaration (temporal dead zone applies), referencing the identifier `CascadeSelect` before its declaration executes throws a `ReferenceError` — unless the Angular linker processes this partial-compilation output (`ɵɵngDeclareFactory`, `ɵɵngDeclareComponent`) into a fully-linked form first, which is presumably not order-sensitive.

This same package builds and tests fine under the classic Karma + `@angular-devkit/build-angular` pipeline, which suggests the linker is applied correctly there but not (or not correctly) for this specific cross-class-reference pattern under the `unit-test` builder in 22.2.0.



### Minimal Reproduction

I don't have an isolated reproduction yet, but you've provided the full trace and the exact line of the affected packet.

### Exception or Error

```text
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'CascadeSelect' before initialization
❯ CascadeSelectSub.<static_initializer> node_modules/@openng/src/cascadeselect/cascadeselect.ts:131:30
❯ node_modules/@openng/src/cascadeselect/cascadeselect.ts:131:39

(Note: the path shown is from the package's sourcemap; the real file evaluated is `node_modules/@openng/optimus-ui/fesm2022/openng-optimus-ui-cascadeselect.mjs`.)
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.0
@angular/build: 22.2.0
Vitest: 5.0.2
Node: v24.21.0
OS: Windows
```

### Anything else relevant?

- The affected npm package is `@openng/optimus-ui` (latest version at time of reporting).
- The broken class is `CascadeSelect` / `CascadeSelectSub`, distributed in Ivy partial-compilation format (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent`, `ɵɵngDeclareFactory`).
- `CascadeSelectSub` is declared earlier in the file than `CascadeSelect`, and its factory's `deps` array references `CascadeSelect` by identifier without going through `forwardRef`.
- This surfaced right after upgrading to 22.2.0, which per the changelog migrated the Angular Linker to oxc-parser/magic-string and included several linker-related fixes in the same release (syntax corruption, parenthesized expressions, source mapping). This may be an edge case not yet covered by the new OXC-based linker implementation.
- Affects every test file whose import graph pulls in this component (via a shared header/footer module), causing the whole suite (not just one test) to fail to load — reported as "(0 test)" by Vitest.

Issues.Title: Server builder assets can overwrite the generated main.js entry point
Issues.Body:
### Command

`build`, `run`

### Is this a regression?

No. The server builder has copied configured assets after Webpack output since the `assets` option was released in 15.1.0.

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

No response.

### Description

`@angular-devkit/build-angular:server` copies configured assets after Webpack emits the server program, without checking whether an asset destination is already a generated file.

With a recursive asset tree copied to output `.`, an asset named `main.js` silently replaces the generated server entry point. The build reports success, and normal `node dist/server/main.js` startup executes the asset instead of the generated application bundle.

I reproduced this with an asset-only dependency update. Version 1.0.0 contains only `assets/data.json`; version 1.0.1 adds only `assets/main.js`. Neither version declares `scripts`, `main`, `exports`, `imports`, or `bin`, installation uses `--ignore-scripts`, and the application never imports the package.

Expected: the build should reject an asset/generated-output collision, or keep generated output authoritative.

Actual: the build succeeds and the final `dist/server/main.js` is byte-for-byte identical to the dependency asset. Starting it executes dependency-controlled code as the deployed server process.

### Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro

```sh
git clone https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro.git
cd angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro
./scripts/validate.sh
```

The validator runs clean → attack → restored-clean → restored-attack. Across two fresh-container runs, clean 1.0.0 always emitted and started the same genuine 782,472-byte bundle with no marker; attack 1.0.1 always emitted the exact 192-byte package asset and executed its marker. Runtime networking is disabled, and the script fails on any control mismatch.

### Exception or Error

No exception is reported. The builder reports successful bundle generation and asset copying.

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.0
@angular-devkit/build-angular: 22.2.0
Angular: 22.2.0
Node: 24.21.0
npm: 11.19.0
OS: Linux arm64 container (node:24.21.0-bookworm-slim)
```

### Anything else relevant?

The builder is deprecated but remains shipped. The default server `assets` list is empty, and exploitation requires an opt-in recursive root-output rule plus an accepted package update, build, deployment, and startup. I therefore assess this as High rather than Critical.

Current source shows the [server builder calling `copyAssets()` after successful Webpack output](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular_devkit/build_angular/src/builders/server/index.ts#L80-L126), while [`copyAssets()` writes each destination without checking generated outputs](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular_devkit/build_angular/src/utils/copy-assets.ts#L41-L60).

This is distinct from #19157 and #16670, which discuss precedence between two configured asset inputs rather than a post-Webpack asset replacing the executable generated entry point.

Should the server builder reject configured asset destinations that collide with generated output files?

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): deduplicate spurious chokidar polling change events
Issues.Body:
When  using Chokidar in polling mode, non-atomic file writes (such as open with O_TRUNC followed by write) can span across poll intervals and cause Chokidar to emit two 'change' events for a single file modification. If the initial rebuild completes quickly (e.g. in JIT mode), the trailing poll event can flush a second rebuild batch with the same file state.

Track the last known mtimeMs and size of watched files in createChokidarWatcher and ignore 'modified' events when the file's mtimeMs and size have not changed since the previous queued or flushed event.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): deduplicate spurious chokidar polling change events" (#34188)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): watchers outside the workspace via parcel didn't work
Issues.Body:
The `dirKey` entry in `this.pendingSubscriptions` caused the following `if` to never be true, as `!this.isCoveredByExistingExternal(dirKey)` is always true as long as `dirKey` is in there. But at this point it isn't pending anymore, as we just `await`ed it the LoC prior.

This bug caused to always run the else which did `sub.unsubscribe()` and killed the just spawned watcher. The effect was, that a directory outside the workspace wasn't watched anymore.

This worked prior to 22.2, but regressed with the switch to the parcel watcher.

See reproduction https://github.com/sod/issue-watcher

Issues.Title: ng build --watch --preserve-symlinks dies with EMFILE when watch mode starts
Issues.Body:
Hi team,

We have one monorepo. A web app and an API both compile a shared model folder. That folder has no `package.json`. The web app reaches it through a symlink, `libs/model`, pointing at `../../model` next to the web app. The watch command is `ng build --watch --preserve-symlinks`. We need `preserveSymlinks` so that link keeps working. On 22.1.7 this watch runs fine.

After moving `@angular/cli` and `@angular/build` to 22.2.0, the bundle still completes (about 92 seconds). Then the process dies as soon as watch mode starts:

```
Watch mode enabled. Watching for file changes...

Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:267:21)
```

The stack goes through chokidar. We're on macOS, Node 24.16.0. `ulimit -n 65536` does not stop it.

22.2 uses chokidar for this case so a directory symlink is still rebuilt. That part is what #34060 fixed for #34039, and the rebuilds do show up. The new problem is everything else the watcher opens. In `setupWatcher`, `**/node_modules/**` is only added to the ignore list when `preserveSymlinks` is false. The comment says that is so `npm link` keeps working. With the flag on, chokidar calls `fs.watch` for every directory under `node_modules`. Ours is large enough that the process runs out of file handles.

This symlink is not an npm link, and it is not inside `node_modules`. Ignoring `node_modules` would still follow `libs/model` to the shared model folder. Could the watcher skip `node_modules` when `preserveSymlinks` is on, and only watch a package that was actually created with `npm link`?

We've gone back to 22.1.7 for now.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "ng build --watch --preserve-symlinks dies with EMFILE when watch mode starts" (#34185)

Issues.Title: feat(@angular/build): add `prerenderFormat` option to prerender routes as `<route>.html`
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

<!-- Please check all that apply using "x". -->

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Prerendering always writes a route to `<route>/index.html`. On static hosts, this forces a choice between clean URLs and no redirects. You can't have both:

- **Clean URLs, but redirects:** links use `/<route>`. Every direct request (search engines, bookmarks, shared links) is first redirected (301/308) to `/<route>/`, and the Angular router then removes the trailing slash again.
- **No redirects, but trailing slashes everywhere:** links have to use `/<route>/`, and the app needs `TrailingSlashPathLocationStrategy` to keep the slash in the address bar.

Issue Number: #29173

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the new behavior that. -->

A new application builder option `prerenderFormat` makes both possible: clean URLs without a trailing slash, served directly with a status code 200.

- `"directory"` (default): `/foo/bar` is written to `foo/bar/index.html`, unchanged.
- `"file"`: `/foo/bar` is written to `foo/bar.html`, so hosts that serve `<route>.html` for `/<route>` respond to `/foo/bar` without a redirect.

Mirrors Astro's `build.format` (`'directory' | 'file'`); Next.js, SvelteKit and Hugo offer the same choice via `trailingSlash`/`uglyURLs`.

- The root route (after removing the `baseHref` option) stays `index.html`, so `/` and `/<locale>/` keep being served by the host's directory index.
- A route that cannot be written safely to `<route>.html` keeps `<route>/index.html`, and the build reports a warning that names the route. This applies to routes whose last segment is `index` in any casing (for example `/index`, `/Index` or `/docs/index`, whose file would be the `index.html` of the parent path), to routes whose file would be the index output of the application (such as `index.csr.html`), and to routes whose file name is already used by another route (compared case-insensitively).
- `"file"` is only considered when the build does not produce a server. The `@angular/ssr` runtime looks up prerendered pages as `<route>/index.html` (`AngularServerApp.buildServerAssetPathFromRequest`, `CommonEngine.retrieveSSGPage`), and with a server there is no redirect to avoid, since the generated `server.ts` serves static files with `redirect: false`. With `outputMode: "server"`, or `ssr` without `outputMode`, the build warns that the option is not considered and prerenders to `<route>/index.html`. The dev server does not prerender and shows no warning.
- It is a top-level option rather than part of `prerender`: when `outputMode` is set, the `prerender` option is not considered ([`options.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular/build/src/builders/application/options.ts#L265-L271)), and `outputMode: "static"` is the documented way to build a fully static application.

As suggested by @SanderElias in the issue, the option description states that not all hosting services support this. Happy to rename the option if you prefer a different name.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

As a stopgap, I built a builder (`@angular-schule/prerender-format`) that wraps `@angular/build:application`. It only works by replacing the internal `prerenderPages()` export of `@angular/build` at runtime to rename the output files, which is fragile and can break with any internal refactoring. A built-in option is the clean solution.

The option description in `schema.json` feeds the `ng build` reference on angular.dev. If this lands, I'm happy to follow up with a short section in the SSR guide ("Generate a fully static application") in angular/angular.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(@angular/build): add `prerenderFormat` option to prerender routes as `<route>.html`" (#34180)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): reset component updates on dev-server SSR page request
Issues.Body:
When server-side rendering is enabled (either internal or external mode), page reload requests are handled by the SSR middleware before reaching the index HTML middleware. As a result, `resetComponentUpdates` was never invoked on page reloads, causing stale component HMR updates to persist in `templateUpdates` and be re-applied over freshly rendered pages.

We now pass `resetComponentUpdates` to `createAngularSsrInternalMiddleware` and `createAngularSsrExternalMiddleware`, and trigger it when an SSR HTML transform occurs (`html:transform:pre`).

Fixes #34163

Issues.Title: docs: resolve guide and doc items in the router
Issues.Body:
`GuideViewer` and `ComponentViewer` looked up their item from the route params themselves, and called `router.navigate` when nothing matched. That meant the component was created and rendered before the redirect, and the redirect started a second navigation.

This moves the lookup into route resolvers. When an item is missing, the resolver returns a `RedirectCommand`, so the router redirects as part of the same navigation, before the component is created. When it's found, the item reaches the component as an input through `withComponentInputBinding()`.

Changes:
- Add `guideResolver` on the `guide/:id` route. It resolves the guide or redirects to `/guides`.
- Add `docItemResolver` on the `:section/:id` route. It resolves the doc item or redirects to the section.
- `GuideViewer`: replace the `id` input and lookup with a required `guide` input, and drop the `Router` and `GuideItems` injections.
- `ComponentViewer`: replace the `id` and `section` inputs and the async lookup with a required `docItem` input. `componentDocItem` is now `toObservable(docItem)`, which replays the latest item like the old `ReplaySubject`, so the child pages are unchanged. The tabs in `sections` become a `computed`, so they're always in the same order instead of depending on the order of previous add/delete calls.

Tests:
- Run the `GuideViewer` and `ComponentViewer` specs against routes that use the resolvers, so they cover both the resolved inputs and the redirects.
- Add a test for the tabs shown for a doc item.

Issues.Title: docs: type the external redirect guard
Issues.Body:
`externalRedirect()` passed its guard to `canActivate` as an inline arrow function. `canActivate` accepts `CanActivateFn` as well as the deprecated class-based guards, typed as `ProviderToken<any>`. Any function also matches `ProviderToken<any>`, so TypeScript didn't check the inline guard against `CanActivateFn`. For example, a guard returning a number would still compile.

This declares the guard as a `CanActivateFn` before passing it to `canActivate`, so its return value is type checked. The behavior is unchanged. A comment explains why the type is needed, so it isn't inlined again later.

Issues.Title: docs: bind route params to component inputs
Issues.Body:
The routed pages in the docs app read their route params by subscribing to `ActivatedRoute` by hand. `ComponentViewer` combined its own params with its parent's to get both `:id` and `:section`, and `ComponentCategoryList` walked `pathFromRoot` and merged the params of every level to find `:section`.

This enables `withComponentInputBinding()` so that the router passes the route params to the routed components as inputs. Nested routes already receive their parent's params, because the router's params inheritance strategy defaults to `always`, so no further router config is needed.

Changes:
- `GuideViewer`: add an `id` input and derive the guide with `computed`. An `effect` sets the page title, or redirects to `/guides` if no guide matches the id.
- `ComponentViewer`: add `id` and `section` inputs and load the doc item from them with `toObservable` and `switchMap`, which still cancels a lookup when the params change before it finishes. The child pages keep reading `componentDocItem`, so they're unchanged.
- `ComponentCategoryList`: add a `section` input and turn the summary and items into signals, updating the template to read them. An `effect` sets the page title.
- Drop the `ActivatedRoute` injections, `combineLatest` and manual param merging from these components.

Tests:
- Rewrite the `GuideViewer` spec with `RouterTestingHarness` and a real route config, and cover the redirect for an unknown guide.
- Add specs for `ComponentViewer` and `ComponentCategoryList` whose routes match the app's nesting (`:section` > sidenav > page). They cover the params reaching the inputs, the page title, and the component being reused and updated when the params change.

Issues.Title: docs: cross-fade between pages with view transitions
Issues.Body:
Navigating between pages in the docs app swapped the content instantly. This enables the router's `withViewTransitions()`, so browsers that support the View Transitions API cross-fade from the old page to the new one. Other browsers keep the current behavior.

Changes:
- Add `withViewTransitions({skipInitialTransition: true})` to the router config. The first page load isn't animated, since there's no previous page to transition from.
- Add a global `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule that disables the view transition animations, so those users get an instant page swap.

Checked in Chrome against the dev server, comparing against a run with `document.startViewTransition` removed to get the behavior without transitions:
- Clicking a category card runs a 250ms cross-fade of the root.
- The first page load doesn't start a transition.
- Focus still moves to the new page's `focusOnNavigation` target.
- Navigating to another page with a `#fragment` still scrolls the target heading into view, at the same position as without transitions.
- With reduced motion, the transition starts but runs no animations.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: cross-fade between pages with view transitions" (#33888)

Issues.Title: docs: update guide viewer title when route params change
Issues.Body:
`GuideViewer` subscribed to the route params to resolve the current guide, but only set the page title once in `ngOnInit`. Since the router reuses the component when only the `:id` param changes, navigating from one guide to another in-app would update the rendered guide while leaving the browser title pointing at the previous one.

This isn't reachable today because guide-to-guide links in the markdown are absolute URLs that trigger a full page load, but it would surface as soon as an in-app link between guides is added.

Changes:
- Set the page title inside the params subscription, next to where the guide is resolved, so both stay in sync on every param emission.
- Remove the now-redundant `ngOnInit` and the `OnInit` interface.
- Tie the params subscription to the component's lifetime with `takeUntilDestroyed()`, matching the pattern used in `ComponentViewer`.
- Switch the spec's mocked `params` to a `BehaviorSubject` and add tests covering the initial title and the title after a param change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "docs: update guide viewer title when route params change" (#33878)

Issues.Title: docs: convert component sidenav guard to a functional guard
Issues.Body: Replaces the class-based `CanActivateComponentSidenav` guard with a functional `CanActivateFn`. Instead of triggering a separate navigation and returning `false`, the guard now returns a `UrlTree` so the router handles the redirect as part of the current navigation.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/drag-drop): avoid rendering pre-drop order in zoneless apps
Issues.Body:
When an item is dropped, the `DropListRef` resets the DOM to its pre-drag order and emits the `dropped` event. With zone.js change detection runs synchronously when the `NgZone` is exited so the new order is rendered before the browser paints. In zoneless apps change detection is scheduled asynchronously which allows the browser to paint the stale order in between, causing the dropped item to blink.

Fixes #33837.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(cdk/drag-drop): avoid rendering pre-drop order in zoneless apps" (#33881)
